clue.text: Hides pains following cold

indicators.note: following tells us the pains come after the cold in the answer

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
pains are aches

explanation.surface: Someone shields their aches after catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to stash it away secretly, as a squirrel stores nuts.

clue.text: Force to include an award for relations

indicators.note: to include says the award is placed inside the word for force

parts.note: to coerce is to force
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: Pressure to give someone a medal for their family links.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade and business dealings between parties; dealings is the sense of relations here.

clue.text: Superficial means of improving the image

definitions.meaning: only on the surface, not deep
a beauty product such as make-up that improves how one looks

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means skin-deep; as a noun it is make-up or a beauty treatment.

clue.text: Discharge when time's up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the word time is taken as written; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Being let out of prison when the sentence is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off or send out, as a chimney gives off smoke.

clue.text: Sneer at a composer of music

indicators.note: a composer puts notes together, so the letters of the preceding words are composed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a writer of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' looks like a person being sneered at, but 'composer of' is the anagram signal working on SNEER AT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenata is an eighteenth-century cantata or instrumental suite, a piece of music.

clue.text: Transport charges?

parts.note: reads as fares for buses and trains, but transport also means delight, so it is fees paid for admission

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' is entrance (to enchant), read as a noun as well; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments made for admission to a venue such as a museum or concert.

clue.text: See some ladies' pyjamas

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to glance at some women's nightwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something.

clue.text: A 16 prepared for flotation

parts.note: 16 points to the solution of 16 down, a word for a management body or to get onto

explanation.surface: A management body ready for a stock market launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flotation' suggests a company going public, but means being afloat on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, which floats, so ready to be carried on the water.

clue.text: Making a request in the manner of royalty

parts.note: as means like or in the manner of
a king is royalty

explanation.surface: Petitioning in a regal style.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a question or plea to someone.

clue.text: A club well-qualified persons run

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, people with good qualifications
hie is an old word meaning hurry or run

explanation.surface: A golf club where highly educated members go for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned iron golf club, roughly equivalent to a five iron.

clue.text: On-and-off restriction of water-usage

parts.note: reads like a hosepipe ban imposed intermittently, but describes a valve that can be turned on or off to control the flow in a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: A tap or valve fitted in a water pipe, opened and closed to start or stop the supply.

clue.text: A bit of chicken and a festive trifle?

parts.note: merry means jolly and festive
a thought means a little, a trifle, as in a thought too salty

explanation.surface: Christmas dinner: some chicken and a seasonal dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the pudding, but means a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the wishbone, the forked bone of a bird's breast pulled for luck.

clue.text: There's need for a break in the garden

indicators.note: break says the word need is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener says it is time to stop for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' reads as a rest from gardening, but signals rearranging NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Support a number, as is permissible

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

explanation.surface: Backing a figure is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is the crossword trick of a Roman numeral: L is fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allowed by law is lawful and permitted.

clue.text: The monarch in a foreign, poetic land

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A king or queen reigns in some faraway land of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic and old name for Ireland, a land foreign to the English setter.

clue.text: Being old, is quite possibly hard

indicators.note: quite possibly says the letters of old and is may be arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: Something aged is likely to be tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and rigid rather than liquid or soft.

clue.text: The management body to get onto

definitions.meaning: a company's directors acting as a governing panel
to climb on to a ship, train or bus

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is the directors of a company; the other is to embark on a vehicle.

clue.text: One whose practice it is to manipulate others

definitions.text: One whose practice it is to manipulate others

parts.words: One whose practice it is to manipulate others
parts.note: suggests a scheming manipulator of people, but describes a therapist who physically manipulates the spine in their clinic

explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats back problems by adjusting the joints and spine by hand.

clue.text: It's doubtful the male worker will accept rest

indicators.note: will accept says the pieces for the male and the worker take another piece inside them

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from the worker ant
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over whether a male employee will agree to a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsure and reluctant, holding back before acting.

clue.text: For sale: ripe produce grown by a nurseryman

indicators.note: produce as a verb means bring forth, so the letters of sale and ripe are brought out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ripe fruit and vegetables advertised for sale by a plant grower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like the noun for fruit and veg, but is the anagram verb working on SALE RIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit tree trained flat against a wall or frame, raised by a plant nursery.

clue.text: Upper-class students

parts.note: suggests posh aristocratic pupils, but means pupils in the most senior class of a British secondary school

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools the sixth form is the final two years before university, the highest class.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in the top two years of a British secondary school, aged sixteen to eighteen.

clue.text: A quarter stepped out at intervals

parts.note: S for south is one of the four quarters of the compass
paced means walked with measured steps

explanation.surface: Someone from one district of a town went for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed with gaps in between, arranged regularly apart.

clue.text: Brags about five family members

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone boasts about the relatives in their family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here; the printed 'few' should read 'five', the Roman V.
explanation.definitionFit: Boasts or shows off about one's achievements.

clue.text: Some people appear allergic to such fruit

indicators.note: Some says only part of the word appear is wanted, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people seem to have an allergy to a particular fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet, juicy orchard fruit, rounded at the bottom and narrowing towards the stalk.

clue.text: Weary of it all, but got through

definitions.meaning: tired and uninterested, sick of everything
drilled through, as a tunnel or hole is made

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is fed up and uninterested; the other is the past tense of drilling a hole.

clue.text: Mail distribution in the capital

indicators.note: distribution spreads the letters of mail around into a new order

explanation.surface: Post being sorted and delivered in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' reads as delivering post, but is the anagram signal for MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Peru, in South America.

clue.text: A noble look

definitions.meaning: a member of the nobility, such as a duke or earl
to gaze closely or squint at something

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is a lord in the House of Lords; the other is to gaze intently.

clue.text: Only a part of some recent investigations

indicators.note: a part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Just a fraction of the latest inquiries.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'investigations' as definition and 'Only a part' as indicator; but 'Only' is the definition (just), and 'a part of' is the hiding signal, leaving 'investigations' as surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Only here means nothing more than, just or simply.

clue.text: Gather to look at the roadside

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or examine carefully
the verge is the grass strip at the side of a road

explanation.surface: People assemble to watch from beside the road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the verge is the grassy edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet at one point, as crowds or lines come together.

clue.text: The Italian, a writer, backing an Asian

indicators.note: backing says the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: il is Italian for the
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An Italian man and a novelist support someone from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole run IL + A + PEN, written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Himalayan country between India and China.

clue.text: Separate the underworld on a Mediterranean island

indicators.note: on says the first piece is placed next to the second, in front of it

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Hades is set apart from a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and individually separate, not continuous; not to be confused with tactful.

clue.text: Home alternative for the shrewd man

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Choosing a house or another option for a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise old king of Pylos in Homer, so a name for any sage elder adviser.
